reviews.title: Turning day into night on Royal Jordanian
reviews.text: Part of the advanced technology on the Boeing 787 Dreamliner is an automated window dimming system, controlled by the captain, in place of the simple shutters which you pushed up or down to control the daylight entering your window. So you have no control over what you can see and are at the mercy of the captain. Return flight from Amman to London left at 12 noon local time and arrived in London at 3 pm local time, the ultimate definition of a daytime flight. We had barely left the Israeli coast before the captain dimmed the windows substantially, and by the time we reached the Dalmatian coast he had locked us down completely as if for a night flight with the windows electronically "closed" When I asked the cabin crew "Why?", I got a waffly reply about some people wanting to sleep and nonsense about protecting the cabin staff from bright sunlight. The windows would be "opened" in about half an hour, but they were finally opened barely in time for us to see the City of London about fifteen minutes from landing. The whole experience was really quite bizarre and it was positively claustrophobic being shut down as if for a night flight on what was actually a beautiful sunny day. Boeing push the Dreamliner as a highly fuel efficient aircraft but with the cabin shut down and all the lights on in broad daylight there is an additional fuel cost. This is truly the most bizarre and ridiculous policy I have ever encountered in over fifty years of flying worldwide. If you are seeking God, you'll find him in the cockpit of a Royal Jordanian Dreamliner, busily turning day into night. If you're not, I would strongly recommend that you never, ever, fly Royal Jordanian.

This completely ruined the end of our holiday due to the stress and upset in trying to get in touch with anyone who could help. We were not given a reason and have still not received one despite asking several times. After complaining we were told that they were glad we understood that flights change (we did not understand and were not given a reason) and that as we were flying to a non EU country we would not be awarded compensation. If you are flying to and from the UK then we would suggest not flying with Royal Jordanian and using an EU carrier in order to be adequately protected. We also do not know if UK flights would be prioritised for bumping and delays due to the absence of protection for the passengers. We would also suggest Royal Jordanian change their literature to reflect this fact.
reviews.author: Helen

reviews.title: Airline excels in service
reviews.text: As with most flights within the Middle East, our trip was relatively short. It was, however, very comfortable and I took the opportunity to chat briefly with the stewardess, who was keen to practice her English. The cabin crew were very conscientious and everything went very smoothly. I must say Royal Jordanian excel in service. It was one of the most pleasant flights we had in our expedition to the Middle East.
reviews.author: Jeffry b

reviews.title: Amman to Tel Aviv was a quick trip
reviews.text: The distances you see on the map in the Middle East can be deceiving. If you say you are flying from Jordan to Israel, it sounds like a long way, but all up the trip is around 30 minutes. Royal Jordanian is very efficient, and it took longer to get from Tel Aviv to Jerusalem than from Amman to Tel Aviv. The Royal Jordanian cabin crew are on the ball. Although the trip was short, we enjoyed it very much.
reviews.author: Jeffry b

reviews.title: Cabin crew are considerate
reviews.text: We transited through Amman several times with Royal Jordanian. We were very pleased at the quality of service. The Amman airport is modern and clean; what's more we had a tasty meal. It was modern Middle Eastern Style; it was very tasty. The cabin crew were very friendly and helpful. They may not get 100% in English, but they get their message across
reviews.author: Jeffry b

reviews.title: I would not recommend
reviews.text: I would not recommend this airline to anyone. They have changed my both my bookings several times, and I wish they at least would change it properly. They only change 1 out of 3 connecting flights. How does that make sense? How am I supposed to get anywhere when they don’t change all of the flights? Then, when I try to contact them, to fix the bookings, they toy me around like an idiot. I go to their office, they tell me to call instead. I call, they set me on hold for several minutes and then tells me to email. I email, they use several days to answer and then tells me to call. I’m actually going crazy dealing with this airline.
reviews.author: Traveling girlie 98

reviews.title: Winner Worst Customer Service Award
reviews.text: I received a phone call at midnight that my 11:25am flight was delayed 5 hours, and was now departing at 5pm. No explanation given and no apologies whatsoever. We lost our connection flight and they didn’t care at all. Since the notification was so late and we had already transportation arrangements we went to the airport as the original check in time. I complained at the check in and asked for an explanation and none was given. I also requested some sort of compensation and the guy laughed at me and said I should speak with the manager. I went to speak with the manager and she offered a snack voucher for a 7 hour wait at the airport. She wasn’t emphatic with our situation, didn’t apologize or seem to try to at least give us an option to make us feel more at ease during our wait for the flight THEY delayed. We even went to their lounge for a day pass so we could be more comfortable for the wait, but they told us we have to wait until it is 3 hours before boarding time in order to use their facilities. So then it’s not a day pass. We’d be paying 30JOD for just three hours when drinks and snacks are not included. They don’t know the meaning of customer service.
reviews.author: dianamar1

reviews.title: Discriminating Airline
reviews.text: This airline is the worst I have seen as a traveler of many other airlines. They have no online check-in and therefore, I got to the gate more than two hours upfront. The guy at the gate (Mo’ayad) told me to come back in 15 minutes only to find out the flight is overbooked. First thing they did was try to make it seem as if overbooked flights are entirely normal and not the airline’s mistake. Second thing I noticed was that they made me wait 15 minutes to let other people in, out of discrimination and choosing who they want to let in and who they want to leave off the flight.
reviews.author: Basel M
